selected.reason: Explicitly shares a correspondent’s grief and traces its effect on others present.

selected.reason: Mothers’ and fathers’ grief broadens the consideration of intimate family loss.

selected.text: Although 'Abdu'l-Baha was saddened by the passing of that exemplar of the people of prostration and that praiseworthy being, He found solace in the devoted efforts of those spiritual friends in the preparation, shrouding and burial of that noble person's remains.

selected.text: How I long to visit that white cemetery! How I yearn to behold that luminous spot

selected.text: Since the day of separation, not a moment passes that you do not come to mind, and not a breath goes by that I do not remember you.

selected.text: Calamities and heart-numbing losses are indeed hard to bear, inasmuch as love and affection torment the heart from the flame of separation.

selected.text: Although a hundred thousand melodies and tunes lie hidden in the recesses of this grief-stricken throat, not one song finds occasion nor one lament finds opportunity.

selected.reason: Recollection of physical mourning practices supplies historical context for comparison with counsel about restraint.

selected.text: O my ancient, divine and spiritual friend! In this morning hour, with the utmost longing I am thinking of you, and I yearned for fellowship and conversation with you. Since this was not possible verbally, I took up pen and paper, finding solace for my heart and soul.
selected.reason: Writing a letter itself brings solace in the absence of conversation and companionship.

selected.text: We are without head or refuge, helpless and remediless. We are wounded by every arrow, and cut by every sword … these broken hearts may find solace, and these withered and dejected souls may find rest and gladness. May this night of sorrows be followed by a bright morn
selected.reason: The movement from a night of sorrow toward a hoped-for dawn gives consolation a sustained image.

selected.text: Make thou no lamentation or cry of grief, but instead chant melodies and raise thy voice in song.
selected.reason: Personal counsel to replace lament with song offers a distinct expressive response requiring context.

selected.text: Due to the delay in the matter of building the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar in that land, much sorrow has resulted for the true friends, for all the peoples in those regions observe that for several years that land has been known as the Temple site yet still nothing has been built.
selected.reason: Disappointment at delayed Temple construction links sorrow with collective effort and responsibility.

selected.text: O let me weep like unto the vernal showers of the Spring! For even the rocks lament on the day of the friends' parting!... … This day is the day of parting. The farewell hour is most difficult to bear. It is the hardest thing in life
selected.reason: Reported farewell joins a poem about spring rain with the difficulty of parting.

selected.text: When she awoke from her dream she prayed: 'O God, the Compassionate! I gave six sons unto Thee. I cannot lose my only son, the last one left to me. Oh spare him! Do not take him also!'
selected.reason: A mother’s prayer after losing six sons presents cumulative bereavement and fear for her surviving child.

selected.text: I was exceedingly sad and heart-broken when I heard of the departure of Mr. Chase, for I loved him very much.
selected.reason: Reported grief at Thornton Chase’s death preserves a specific friendship and remembrance.

selected.text: their celebration by us are always shaded with a recurring sad recollection
selected.reason: Recurring sadness during celebration raises the connection between festivals and remembered loss.

selected.text: "I pray you remove my doubt, and give me consolation, I have lost my beloved husband."
selected.reason: A widow directly asks for consolation and removal of doubt; the complete exchange is central.

selected.text: And my sorrow is for the dwellers of the house, that no grief should befall them
selected.reason: The Báb expresses concern that grief should not befall a household, adding a personal protective concern.

selected.text: By God! We hear the lamentation of the pulpits saying: "O my God! O Lord! Deliver us from these embodiments of tyranny and oppression, and adorn us with Thy near servants and sincere trusted ones
selected.reason: The lament of pulpits personifies sorrow over the misuse of religious speech.

selected.text: The mention of loved ones is the key that opens the door of sorrow, and the countenance of the friends is the dawning-place of light in the darkness of the world.
selected.reason: Remembrance opens sorrow while the friends’ presence brings light, preserving the relationship’s complexity.

selected.text: The love of children is a natural and mighty thing, and the cause and reason for its manifestation hath generally been due to external causes, for man hath loved and loveth the perpetuation of his name and mention, and the cause of this, in the sight of God and men, is primarily the perpetuation of traces, and children are reckoned as the greatest of man's traces. selected.reason: A substantive explanation of parental love and grief after reunion supplies an important conceptual passage.

selected.text: Thou didst desire to attain His presence; however, due to the great distance and the opposition of the deniers and the objections of the oppressors, this matter is now postponed.
selected.reason: Postponed meeting due to distance and opposition preserves the practical causes of separation.

selected.text: We testify that through our heedlessness the pillars of unity have been shaken in Thy lands and the banners of detachment in Thy realm. selected.reason: A prayer acknowledges collective responsibility amid invasion and loss, joining lament with self-examination.

selected.text: We console you through the fragrances of My utterance and the sweet-scented breezes of My verses, and comfort you through My grace and My mercy which have preceded all things great and small
selected.reason: Consolation through utterance, verses, grace and mercy directly addresses how comfort is offered.

selected.text: O My handmaiden! O My handmaiden! Rise above the ranks of grief and sadness and turn to the horizon of sanctification, detachment and transcendence. selected.reason: A distinctive qualification about sorrow and the Sun of Truth requires full context alongside the diverse expressions of grief.

selected.text: It has been a long time since this evanescent servant was separated from you in exile. But in truth, you took joy with you. What I mean by these words is that after you left, joy became very rare, like the phoenix in all regions and cities. And that joy, in reality, did not even go with you - it was very unfaithful, for it left us and did not accompany you either. Surely you too were saddened by separation from the Beloved of all horizons.
selected.reason: A personal letter describes joy departing with the absent friend, giving separation a relational voice.

selected.text: The Maid of Heaven hath wailed in the most exalted Paradise, and the tears of dawn are her weeping. The heaven of existence hath changed by reason of what hath befallen it, and the redness visible on the horizon is its sighing.
selected.reason: Dawn and the redness of the horizon become images of cosmic mourning in a distinctive passage.

selected.text: O My Sister! By God, I have so blotted out from memory the remembrance of everything that I know not what hath been written down. Sorrow hath so surrounded Me that I have forgotten Mine own Self, how much more the writing of letters. O that My Mother had never given birth to Me
selected.reason: A letter to Bahá’u’lláh’s sister gives unusually direct expression to grief, impaired writing and the wish not to have been born.

selected.text: Thou seest my poverty and neediness, my weakness and brokenness, my distress and anguish, my sorrow and tribulation. It is as though Thou hast closed the doors of Thy mercy upon the face of Thy servant, cast him out from the vicinity of Thy sovereignty, expelled him from the paradise of Thy holy bounty, and distanced him from Thy grace and favor.
selected.reason: Prayer voices the experience of closed doors of consolation and perceived distance from divine favor.

selected.text: Alas, alas! O God of Mercy … But today who can console Thee in this calamity before which all calamities bow down, and this sorrow which hath stunned all sorrows
selected.reason: Asks who can console the one who consoles others, a distinctive theological and relational question.

selected.text: O servant! When you find yourself alone in your house, then remember My loneliness. And if you find sorrow in yourself, then reflect on My sorrows. And if you journey to other lands, then remember My exile and My tribulation.
selected.reason: Connects a reader’s loneliness, sorrow and travel with remembrance of the Manifestation’s experience.

selected.text: the Wronged One is in such grief as the eye of creation hath never beheld its like … Although sorrows have encompassed Us, yet the grief of the world hath not, and will not, prevent the Lord of ancient days from His Cause
selected.reason: Holds encompassing grief together with persistence in the work of the Cause.

selected.text: Rejoice thou in the gladness of God, though He Who biddeth thee rejoice is himself in such sorrow that the Trees of Oneness have been deprived of their fruits.
selected.reason: The invitation to rejoice comes from one who explicitly acknowledges His own sorrow.

selected.text: This is a Book from the Primal Point unto her who hath believed in God her Lord, and who hath lamented in His separation and wept at His parting and cried out in His remoteness
selected.reason: A text voiced from the Primal Point to a grieving believer preserves a distinctive devotional address.

selected.text: Many a true morn has dawned, yet the night of separation has not ended. How many nightingales have burst into song in the gardens, yet no bird has warbled a melody from the city of reunion. It seems the gates of hope have closed and the gardens of despair have opened.
selected.reason: The prolonged night of separation persists despite successive mornings, expressing grief’s altered sense of time.

selected.text: Thou seest the Countenance of Justice beneath the claws of tyranny, and the Temple of Unity in the hands of the idolaters. O Lord! The days of oppression have lengthened, though Thou didst promise in the Book their brevity, and the times of hardship have extended, though Thou didst pledge that ease would accompany them.
selected.reason: Lament appeals to the promise of ease while acknowledging prolonged oppression.

selected.text: the Wronged One remembereth every wronged man and woman, and the Stranger loveth every stranger, man and woman, and every captive man and woman
selected.reason: The Wronged One’s care extends explicitly to wronged people, strangers and captives of both sexes.

selected.text: Each day doth the wolf devour one of the sheep of God. O my God! How long wilt Thou look on and be patient?
selected.reason: The question how long addresses divine patience amid continuing harm to the innocent.

selected.text: Nevertheless, this imprisoned one is troubled and is reminded of this word: that we have always been content with news of your honor, but now the messenger is forbidden and that blessing is cut off.
selected.reason: Restriction on messengers and news makes the practical isolation of imprisonment explicit.

selected.text: The Blessed Beauty was so affected and saddened by this event that for nine full days no one was granted permission to attain His presence.
selected.reason: A reported nine-day withdrawal after grievous news gives mourning a specific temporal and personal setting.

selected.text: "O God! selected.reason: An anguished prayer seeks release from weakness and burdens; its full historical and devotional context is essential.

selected.text: Tell Jinab-i-Murtada-Quli Mirza on my behalf to raise up a balanced figure like his father and not be sorrowful
selected.reason: Counsel to a son connects consolation with continuing a father’s qualities.

selected.text: They have left behind on Thy earth weak offspring who are captives in the hands of the most wicked among Thy creation and the tyrants of Thy realm. They have become hungry, thirsty, naked and barefoot in Thy realm.
selected.reason: A prayer explicitly names surviving children’s hunger, thirst and lack of clothing, centering practical vulnerability.

selected.text: When this news reached the sacred court, it had such an effect that those who learned of it concealed it, and those who heard it kept it hidden and concealed, lest the blessed leaf hear of it and begin sighing and lamenting with tearful eyes, burning heart and consuming soul, and become companion to wailing and moaning, causing great anguish and severe distress.
selected.reason: Concealment of distressing news raises a concrete question about care, communication and its effects.

selected.text: By the life of God, Fatima the Radiant wept for you in the Garden of Refuge, and the Most Exalted Woman cried and lamented over your oppression in the highest Paradise, and the Greater Mary wailed in grief for you in the verdant gardens, and Sarah and Eve shed flowing tears for you like rain from heaven.
selected.reason: Women of sacred history participate in mourning, broadening the guide’s scriptural and symbolic frame.

selected.text: As for Abu'l-Fadl, praise be to God, in his own time, as soon as news of his death spread to distant cities, people mourned and shed tears, joined in sighs and laments, and sought the elevation of his station in their prayers
selected.reason: The response to Abu’l-Fadl’s death joins widespread mourning with prayers for his spiritual progress.

selected.text: Consider what calamity I face. Reflect a little that some friends, instead of striving to place a balm on this wound, secretly sprinkle salt. How then is there opportunity or possibility for writing?
selected.reason: The image of adding salt to a wound makes friends’ responsibility toward a grieving person concrete.

selected.text: The terrible and shocking news of the new calamity has saddened hearts and grieved souls. Truly this calamity is severe
selected.reason: Names the shock of a new calamity and its communal emotional effects.

selected.text: it has been some time since Hadrat-i-Fadil has been away from you, and separation and estrangement cause great sorrow, especially for two souls who are joined heart, body and spirit in each other's embrace. However much you lament and cry out, you are justified.
selected.reason: Explicitly validates a separated spouse's lament and the closeness of their bond.

selected.text: Its review caused much grief and sorrow - how the former unfaithful ones destroyed that magnificent building and took its doors, windows and roof timbers to build houses for themselves. How regrettable this is.
selected.reason: Grief over the destruction and appropriation of a cherished building broadens loss beyond bereavement.

selected.text: Your letter was read and recited with utmost grief and sorrow. It had a profound effect and ignited a fire in the heart. Truly you are oppressed and in God's path the target of the arrow of calamity and pierced by the dart of cruelty. Every oppressed one weeps for your oppression and every sorrowful one begins lamentation and moaning for your sorrow. Whatever cry and wail you make, you have the right.
selected.reason: Expressly acknowledges oppression and the sufferer's right to cry and lament.

selected.text: From that day until the day of separation, by your precious life O kind friend, I did not draw one breath in peace, found not a moment's rest, and was held back from service, for he kept me occupied. … This is the heartache that I share with that old friend, that he may be my partner and companion in this grief and sorrow
selected.reason: Describes sustained unrest and asks for companionship within sorrow.

selected.text: But the friends attend the procession sorrowful and grief-stricken, regretful and remorseful, becoming intercessors and begging forgiveness.
selected.reason: Places sorrow and intercession within the concrete setting of a funeral procession.

selected.text: At times He is silent, the cord of hope broken, freed from attachment to all else, wounded by the arrow of cruelty. At times in the dark night, companion to tearful eyes, lamenting cries and a burning heart. Sometimes raising loud cries of anguish and grief, other times passing time depressed, withered and hurt.
selected.reason: Depicts changing emotional states and exhausted hope across time.

selected.text: All these tribulations came in succession, following one after another after the passing of that ascended spouse, and beyond these, countless afflictions assailed thee, and I am aware of them all.
selected.reason: Recognizes cumulative adversity following the death of a spouse.

selected.text: I had no comfort in this great convulsion and this overwhelming, devastating calamity which shook my pillars and limbs, melted my liver and heart, and obliterated my being and essence … Thou knowest well, O fiery phoenix, the intensity of my separation, the severity of my burning, my excessive yearning, my sighing and moaning, the flame of my fire, the clamor of my heart and the blazing of my fires from this grief which has crushed my bones and melted my flesh and innards
selected.reason: Names bodily devastation and the need for comfort following overwhelming loss.

selected.text: O my God! You know my sorrow and grief, my burning anguish and sadness in these days. I cannot pour out my grief and sorrow and complaint to anyone but You.
selected.reason: Offers direct prayer as a place for grief that cannot be confided elsewhere.

selected.text: The ascension of His honor Haji Mirza 'Abdullah caused the utmost sorrow. The soul and heart of this wronged one became so grieved that it cannot be expressed … The loss of such a blessed soul certainly causes grief, and this sorrow will ever remain and endure and never be forgotten
selected.reason: Acknowledges lasting sorrow and enduring remembrance after a particular death.

selected.text: when she heard the news of the death of him who ascended to God, Mirza Ahmad, she wept and lamented continuously at night for a full year
selected.reason: Records a full year of repeated mourning rather than assuming a brief uniform response.

selected.text: Alas, alas, the trees lament thy separation, the flowers thy departure, and the two rivers thy absence. The other gardens and all the orchards of the earth have seized thee.
selected.reason: Uses trees, flowers and rivers as a distinctive poetic language of separation.

selected.text: he is unwell and after having been wealthy has become destitute
selected.reason: Connects emotional distress with illness and the material loss of livelihood.

selected.text: Due to the intensity of its effect, I did not write a response until now, for if I had written, it would have increased the grief and sorrow of that beloved of hearts, and the reins of the pen would have slipped from my hand. Thus, silence was necessarily chosen. selected.reason: Explains delayed correspondence as care against intensifying another person's grief.

selected.text: However, the painful events in those vast territories caused extreme sorrow. … Glory be to God! What ignorance is this that humans are predatory toward one another and bloodthirsty
selected.reason: Connects grief at public violence with a critique of human cruelty.

selected.text: I observed a group of people, grief-stricken and heartbroken, weeping and lamenting, engaged in reciting elegies for the Prince of Martyrs (peace be upon him), crying out: "O Husayn, what did they do when they made thee a sacrifice
selected.reason: Provides a concrete scene of communal elegy and remembrance of Husayn.

selected.text: Do not be sorrowful and grieved by the great calamities that have befallen you. Every breast is a target for the arrow of tribulation, and every heart is afflicted with some sorrow
selected.reason: Situates personal calamity within a shared human experience of sorrow.

selected.text: I have the utmost love for you and my longing to meet you is also endless, but at present wisdom does not permit it
selected.reason: Shows longing for reunion alongside practical limits on an immediate visit.

selected.text: I am now so sorrowful and grief-stricken that my fingers can no longer write - my hands are trembling. Consider then how sorrowful and heartsick I am.
selected.reason: Records grief that interrupts the physical act of writing.

selected.text: Although compelling occupations and pressing duties surround me from all directions at present, and there is absolutely no opportunity to write even a word, yet since you are related to that essence of purity and that pearl of the shell of faithfulness - he who was a martyr to the Blessed Beauty and a sacrifice to the Exalted One, detached from all else, ascended to the Abha Kingdom, and attained the paradise of reunion - I have put aside all tasks and turned to remembering you
selected.reason: Gives remembering a distant friend priority amid pressing duties.

selected.text: It is the season of festival, yet we are hopeless of seeing the Beloved … The world is in feasting and drinking, while we have tear-filled eyes
selected.reason: Contrasts a public festival with private grief through a poetic voice.

selected.text: How long will you remain submerged in the sea of sorrows? Have you, like this 'Abdu'l-Baha, been afflicted by the cruelty of brothers
selected.reason: Raises the distinctive wound of cruelty within a family.

selected.text: Thy letter arrived and I became saddened by the distressing news about thy dear son's condition.
selected.reason: Addresses distress concerning a living son's condition, extending care beyond bereavement.

selected.text: It is clear from Amin's letter that he has become saddened. What is the cause of this sadness? Write what you have
selected.reason: Asks about the cause of sadness instead of presuming to know it.

selected.text: I arrived in New York. However, I was not for a moment free of My thoughts for all of you, especially for Ruha Khanum and Shoghi Effendi, particularly when remembering Ruha's weeping and lamentation as she lay gravely sick in bed
selected.reason: Connects travel and public service with continuing concern for sick family members.

selected.text: I too am kind to that guest, for he awakens me at midnight and makes me remember the friends.
selected.reason: Uses a nocturnal visitor as an unexpected occasion for remembering friends.

selected.text: A poem in Turkish has been composed commemorating your loss which is enclosed with this letter.
selected.reason: Names a commemorative Turkish poem as an act of consolation.

selected.text: On account of the death of thy father and brother the utmost sorrow and regret was produced. How unfortunate it is that that young man was killed instantly by the sudden shock!
selected.reason: Acknowledges the double loss of father and brother and a sudden death.

selected.text: O servant of the Threshold of the Friend! selected.reason: Questions the limits of words in soothing grief while attempting a caring response.

selected.text: This was distressing news, and therefore a telegram was immediately sent from Egypt to inquire, but no reply has yet been received, causing concern.
selected.reason: Responds to distress with an immediate practical inquiry and sustained concern.

selected.text: For some time now the birds of the meadow have ceased their songs of praise. This is due to the requirements of this season
selected.reason: Uses seasonal silence to describe a pause in expressions of praise.

selected.text: In this supreme calamity and grievous tribulation that hath befallen the servants of the Most Glorious Beauty and the handmaids of the All-Merciful in the path of the Lord of Grandeur, thou too hast received an abundant share and hast endured severe persecution from thy kindred and tribe.
selected.reason: Includes a woman's suffering from her own kin and tribe in a prayerful response.

selected.text: Your cries and complaints and sighs and lamentations and wailing are all justified and you are right - truly you have been left alone
selected.reason: Directly recognizes the justice of lament in the condition of being left alone.

selected.text: Regarding thy extreme sorrow, thy sadness and thy great regret for My imprisonment, there is no harm therein.
selected.reason: Explicitly permits sorrow over imprisonment, balancing other admonitions against grief.

selected.text: O thou gentle soul that showeth kindness to the bereaved! In truth thy services to the bereaved family of the martyrs hath caused me untold happiness.
selected.reason: Praises practical service to a bereaved family as a source of happiness.

selected.text: The Ancient Beauty of Canaan, in separation from Joseph of Egypt, shed tears of blood from his eyes and wept so much that "his eyes became white with sorrow, and he was suppressed with grief."
selected.reason: Explicitly evokes Jacob's tears for Joseph, a distinctive scriptural image of grief.

selected.text: Deal not with any steadfast soul in such wise as to cause him to become sorrowful and distressed
selected.reason: States an ethical responsibility to avoid causing another person distress.

selected.text: Thou hadst expressed grief and sorrow at the ascension of the blessed temple of Ibn-i-Abhar. selected.reason: Explains how one death can represent a loss felt by an entire community.

selected.text: until her bones grew frail, her hair turned white, her strength failed, and the brilliant flower withered from successive pains and recurring illnesses.
selected.reason: Recognizes ageing, recurring illness and successive pains in a woman's life.

selected.text: Although you two sisters from the beginning endured utmost persecution from the enemies of the Beauty of Abha, and in every breath the poison of oppression and enmity affected your being, though you became the target of the arrow of cruelty
selected.reason: Addresses two sisters together and acknowledges their continuing persecution.

selected.text: Not for a moment did she find peace of soul or tranquility of conscience. The trauma of the martyrdom of the Bab on one hand, countless afflictions on another, and the attacks of enemies on yet another
selected.reason: Remembers the prolonged suffering of a woman after the Bab's martyrdom.

selected.text: We have written an elegy for him which, if recited upon rock would melt it, upon rivers would freeze them, upon dust would ignite it, upon heaven would make it weep, and upon earth would make it lament.
selected.reason: Describes an elegy's emotional power through a sustained series of natural images.

selected.text: provided that you can allay the complaints of his wife so that she will have no cause for lamentation and cry
selected.reason: Makes attention to a wife's distress a condition within a practical request.

selected.text: At times I felt so weak and feeble by this 'nerve agitation' that I was unable to speak even one word. I did not say anything to anyone, but I suffered often for hours.
selected.reason: A reported account names concealed suffering and the disabling effects of nervous agitation.

selected.text: Whenever I think of our last meeting my heart is filled with sadness. It is now a little less than fifty years and still that youth is living in my memory, as though it was a matter of yesterday.
selected.reason: A reported memory retains the freshness of sorrow after almost fifty years.

selected.text: The people are suffering greatly because all their children have been taken for military service.
selected.reason: A reported observation connects family suffering with compulsory military service.

selected.text: Now say whatever your troubled heart desires. It is obvious what state came over you with all those favors and kindnesses.
selected.reason: A reported invitation gives the troubled person space to speak freely.

selected.text: O thou human being! Grieve not for anything, for thy grief causeth Me grief, and weep not for anything, for thy weeping causeth Me to weep. No word hath issued forth from Me regarding thy station, for I love thee. Therefore stand firm in what thou art
selected.reason: Presents divine sympathy through the language of another's tears causing reciprocal tears.

selected.text: And regarding the ascension of the illustrious Siyyid [Kazim] - may God exalt his station - which you had mentioned, I clothed all my being in the garment of grief. We are from God and to Him do we return, in submission to God's decree and yielding to His command
selected.reason: The Bab explicitly joins mourning for Siyyid Kazim with submission to God's decree.

selected.text: From Shiraz my mother -- may she be illumined -- sendeth word: May my soul be a ransom for thee! From the hour of sunset, honored with the bounty of Presence, until now -- which is the afternoon of Thursday, the twenty-eighth of the blessed month of Sha'ban -- praise and thanksgiving be to God, all that God ordained for me hath passed
selected.reason: Preserves a mother's voice within correspondence and a specific account of distress.

selected.text: the Most Sorrowful, the Most Sorrowful! … Verily doth Joy proclaim: "My soul be a sacrifice to Thy sorrow, O Thou Who art wronged by the peoples of the world!" Rest doth speak and call out: "My reality be a sacrifice to Thy tribulation, O Thou Who art the Rest of all mankind
selected.reason: Personifies Joy and Rest in relation to sorrow and tribulation.

selected.text: In brief, the surging waves of separation are not yet stilled - at every moment they appear with new force and in different form. The separation from Ali hath wrought and continueth to work such effects.
selected.reason: Describes grief as recurring waves that appear with differing force and form.

selected.text: Blessed art thou for having been seized with grief when thou didst learn what hath befallen the Wronged One in this manifest prison. By My life, were I to lift the veil, the lamentation of weeping would be raised between the heavens and the earth
selected.reason: Pronounces a blessing on grief and tears at another's imprisonment.

selected.text: thee be the peace of God, Lord of all worlds! What hath befallen thee hath grieved Me to such an extent that for several days I laid down My pen
selected.reason: Shows another person's affliction interrupting the writer's work for several days.

selected.text: O City of God! How canst thou endure this separation that sets Iraq ablaze and melts the horizons … O land of the City! How can roses appear from thee and plants of glory spring forth after the disappearance of God's rose, the Transcendent, the Luminous
selected.reason: Addresses a city directly as a mourner of separation and departure.

selected.text: I testify that through you the Divine Lote Tree lamented and the hearts of those who cast away the world and turned to the highest horizon in the days of God, Lord of the Throne and earth, were melted. … Thus has the Pen spoken from the station whereon the Lord of eternity was established upon His mighty throne. selected.reason: Connects present mourning with the Virgin and the Messenger in sacred remembrance.

selected.text: This Wronged One is in truth despairing of the peoples of the earth … What more can this Wronged One mention, and to whom shall He speak? Reflect a little on what was mentioned, that thou mayest lament the state of this Wronged One and realize the depths of His despair
selected.reason: Voices profound disappointment with humanity and the difficulty of communicating it.

selected.text: and he lamented with the lamentation of those who have lost. … O servant! Know thou that thy yearning in separation from the Luminary of the horizons when He departed from the precincts of Iraq was greater in the sight of God than the worship of most of the servants
selected.reason: Assigns religious value to yearning in separation through a direct comparison with worship.

selected.text: In truth, after your departure the prison truly became a prison. Some are occupied with lamentation and moaning, while others are consumed by the fire of separation.
selected.reason: Makes a companion's departure change the felt experience of imprisonment.

selected.text: In such days grievous news arrived from that land which added to Our sorrows. Ibn Farid says: "My grief - Jacob did not reveal the least of it, and all of Job's afflictions were but a portion of my tribulation."
selected.reason: Explicitly quotes Ibn Farid's comparison with Jacob and Job, preserving a literary point of contact.

selected.text: God, exalted be His glory, commandeth thee to be patient. Verily He is the All-Patient and commandeth His servants and handmaidens to show beautiful patience amid the vicissitudes of the world and the passing of nations.
selected.reason: Counsels beautiful patience amid changing circumstances and public upheaval.

selected.text: By My life! I rejoice in your joy and am saddened by your sadness. … Let not My guest become sorrowful. Always console him on behalf of God, and likewise the other relatives
selected.reason: Moves from shared joy and sorrow to an instruction to console a guest and relatives.

selected.text: We make mention of grief to manifest My grace, My mercy and My loving-kindness
selected.reason: Explains the mention of grief in terms of grace, mercy and loving-kindness.

selected.text: By the life of God! A pure deed endureth and lasteth, and remaineth and speaketh throughout centuries and ages
selected.reason: Offers the lasting effects of a pure deed as a distinct response to loss.

selected.text: By Thy glory, in this moment the breeze of despair has wafted, O Hope of the worlds! Thou seest how anxiety and agitation have seized me, O my Lord, the All-Bestowing!
selected.reason: Addresses the Hope of the worlds while naming present despair and anxiety.

selected.text: O servant! Hear My call, then grieve thou with My grief and imprisonment. By God! No greater tribulation hath befallen My soul than that which hath befallen My loved ones, if ye be of them that understand.
selected.reason: Identifies loved ones' suffering as the speaker's greatest tribulation.

selected.text: no troubles of the realm shall touch him save separation from the Beloved. But since this is by God's decree, he accepteth it, yet remembereth it throughout the months and years.
selected.reason: Holds acceptance of divine decree together with remembrance over months and years.

selected.text: These are the days of farewell, and grief hath seized the people of God, for the Fast, which was the cause of refinement and the means of reformation and spirituality of souls, hath come to an end. This separation consumeth the lovers and demolisheth the pillars of patience.
selected.reason: Locates farewell and grief in the ending of the Fast and its spiritual practices.

selected.text: The vicissitudes of time, which have appeared through God's irrevocable decrees, have separated companions who shared the same nest, and what beloved ones have been separated from their Beloved, and what lovers have been consumed in separation from their Loved One!
selected.reason: Uses companions of one nest to evoke separation through the vicissitudes of time.

selected.text: O Lord! The sorrowful one hath clung to Thy Name, the Joy-Giving, and the grief-stricken to Thy Name, the All-Subduing over all names.
selected.reason: Contrasts felt sorrow with an appeal to the divine name Joy-Giving.

selected.text: The sorrows that have come have rolled up the carpet of joy. Glory be to God! At one moment my heart rejoiceth because of it, and at another I find it in manifest grief. The poet of Shiraz hath well said: … "If the wind were to fall upon me it would carry me away, … for no one remaineth beneath this garment
selected.reason: Preserves a poetic movement between joy, sorrow and self-effacement.

selected.text: and then clothes itself in the black garment in their mourning
selected.reason: Includes the distinctive image or practice of a black garment of mourning.

selected.text: Let nothing grieve thee save separation from Me, the Inaccessible, the Forbidden, and complain thou of naught save thy remoteness from My presence, for this is the root of sorrow, which none save those nigh unto God can comprehend.
selected.reason: Explicitly restricts sorrow to spiritual separation, requiring careful comparison with validating passages.

selected.text: O Lord! The necks of hypocrisy have grown long, and the clouds of darkness have encompassed the Daystar of the horizons. I implore Thee by Thine own wronged state and the wronged state of Thy loved ones to assist Thine enemies to act with justice and fairness.
selected.reason: Turns the suffering of the wronged into a prayer for enemies to act justly.

selected.text: My heart lamenteth and Mine eye weepeth, yet the tongue speaketh in praise of the All-Merciful amidst the concourse of all worlds
selected.reason: Directly joins lamenting heart and weeping eye with spoken praise.

selected.text: Due to my weakness, my abasement, my poverty, my evanescence, my powerlessness, my suffering, my loneliness and my tribulation, my tongue is tied, my heart is melted, and my limbs tremble. O Lord! Affairs have become severe for me, faces have grown cheerless, souls are choking, breasts are constricted, and adversaries have laid snares of cunning and guile for these birds whose wings are broken by the arrows of cruelty.
selected.reason: Joins personal weakness and grief with intercession for others whose wings are broken.
